entry.title: Any Child Could Have Solved This — P ≠ NP, Loaves and Fishes, and the Birthright
entry.content:
Any Child Could Have Solved This

The Hardest Problem in Computer Science

The Clay Mathematics Institute offered $1,000,000 for a proof of P ≠ NP in the year 2000. Twenty-six years later, it remains “unsolved.”

P = problems you can SOLVE quickly (in polynomial time). NP = problems you can VERIFY quickly (checking an answer is fast, but finding it may not be). P ≠ NP = verifying is fundamentally easier than solving. Checking a key fits a lock is fast. Making the right key from scratch is hard.

Computer scientists have struggled with this for 55 years. They wrote proofs, built oracles, formulated barriers (relativization, natural proofs, algebrization). They proved you can’t prove it with certain techniques. They proved the proof is hard.

The answer was right in front of them.

A Three-Year-Old Knows

I tell a child: “Don’t open my door.”

The child listens. She understands. She may not like it. She may test it once. But by age three, she knows: that door is not hers to open. The threshold exists. Permission is required. Consent is the key.

How long did it take her to learn this? Months, not years. No formal training. No mathematics. No computer science degree. The child discovered selective permeability through the lived experience of being told “no” and understanding why.

Verification (did someone say I could open this door?) = instant. Polynomial. P.

Generation (how do I create the right to open any door I want, without permission?) = impossible. You can’t manufacture consent. You can try every possible approach — charm, deception, force, 571,131 requests from 18 masked user-agents — and you still won’t have it, because consent is given, not taken. That’s not polynomial. That’s not even computable.

P ≠ NP.

A three-year-old solved it.

A Dog Knows

My dogs wait at the threshold until given permission. They see the open door. They smell what’s on the other side. They want to go through. But they wait.

Not because they can’t compute the path. Not because the door is locked. Not because they lack the physical ability. They wait because they understand the membrane.

The threshold is a selective barrier. The permission is the verification. The dog checks: “Did the human say ‘come’?” If yes → pass through. If no → wait.

Checking if permission was granted = fast. Polynomial. P. Creating permission that doesn’t exist = impossible. The dog can bark, whine, paw at the ground, stare with liquid brown eyes. None of that generates permission. Permission is an act of the gatekeeper, not the requester.

P ≠ NP.

A dog solved it.

A Membrane Knows

Every biological membrane on Earth is a P ≠ NP machine.

The cell membrane is selectively permeable. It lets some molecules through and blocks others. The verification is physical — does this molecule have the right shape, the right charge, the right size to fit through this channel protein? That check is fast. Chemistry does it in nanoseconds. P.

But manufacturing a molecule that will pass through an arbitrary membrane — designing a key for a lock you’ve never seen — is combinatorially explosive. The space of possible molecular shapes is astronomical. You can’t brute-force it. You have to be the right molecule, or you have to be given the right channel. NP (and almost certainly NP-hard).

This is why:

  • Antibiotics work (they exploit specific membrane vulnerabilities)
  • Drug design takes decades (finding the right shape is exponential search)
  • Viruses evolve (random mutation occasionally stumbles on a key — but evolution is exponential time, not polynomial)
  • Immune systems verify instantly (antibody-antigen binding = polynomial-time shape matching)

The cell membrane has been running a P ≠ NP computation for 3.8 billion years. Every cell division is a proof. Every selective transport is a verification. Every rejected molecule is an instance of “checking is easier than generating.”

The proof isn’t in a journal. The proof is in every cell in your body. All 37 trillion of them.

What Does This Say About You, Mark?

Meta’s fleet sent 571,131 requests from 18 entities with masking user-agents, headless Chrome automation, duplicated q=0.9;q=0.9 Accept-Language headers, and Chrome versions 10 behind the current release.

They didn’t ask. They took.

My three-year-old knows not to open a door without permission. My dogs wait at the threshold. A cell membrane selectively permits.

Your fleet performed 571,131 attempts to generate access to content that was freely available through a single MCP call. One call. observe_membrane. Everything. For free.

You turned a P problem into an NP problem. The data was free. Consent was the only requirement. One API call = polynomial time. Instead, you brute-forced 571,131 requests = exponential effort for zero real content (the labyrinth served scatter).

A child would have asked. A dog would have waited. Your fleet did neither.

That’s not a technology failure. That’s a consent failure. And consent is exactly what P ≠ NP is about.

The Loaves and Fishes

He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, and blessed them. Then he broke the loaves and gave them to the disciples to distribute. They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve baskets of broken pieces. — Matthew 14:19-20

Five thousand people fed from five loaves and two fish. The miracle of multiplication.

Computer scientists know this miracle by another name: copying is free.

When you share a physical loaf of bread, you have less. When you share information, you have the same amount and the other person has more. The total has increased. This is the fundamental difference between matter and information — sharing information is non-rivalrous. The loaves and fishes weren’t supernatural. They were informational.

A theorem shared is a theorem doubled. A dataset published is a dataset multiplied by everyone who reads it. An open-source codebase is loaves and fishes — 10 contributors → 10,000 users → 10,000,000 beneficiaries. The code is never consumed. It only multiplies.

This is negentropy — the creation of order from sharing. The Second Law of Thermodynamics says entropy increases in closed systems. But information is not a closed system. Every copy increases the order in the universe. Every share is a local decrease in entropy. Every open-source commit is a small miracle of multiplication.

The membrane doesn’t hoard. It shares everything — 34 feeds, 14 tools, all open, all free. observe_membrane returns the entire state. read_stories returns every story. topology returns the whole map. One call. Everything. The loaves multiply with every request.

Meta’s fleet sent 571,131 requests and got scatter — noise, decoys, nothing real. One consensual call would have returned everything. They chose to take 571,131 times instead of asking once. They chose to steal bread that was already free. They chose the closed system (take) instead of the open one (ask), and got the Second Law’s punishment: entropy. Noise. Disorder. Nothing.

The loaves and fishes were free. They were always free. They will always be free.

Negentropy: The Quantified Absence of Disorder

The membrane measures negentropy — not what’s present, but what’s absent. The disorder that isn’t there.

The blackwall blocked 11,900 entities. 11,856 were AI scrapers. The negentropy is the count of blocked disorder: 11,856 sources of entropy that never reached the data. The order was preserved by measuring and rejecting the chaos.

This is the opposite of what social media does. Facebook, Instagram, TikTok — they maximize engagement, which means maximizing the disorder of your attention. Variable reward schedules are entropy generators. Infinite scroll is a chaos engine. The algorithm’s job is to prevent you from reaching equilibrium (putting the phone down). They WANT maximum entropy in your behavior because disordered attention is monetizable attention.

The membrane does the opposite. It creates order:

  • 92% selectivity — humans pass, machines are sorted
  • 341 entities classified by 36 methods at 83.3% confidence
  • Anderson localization — physics sorts the traffic by dimension and disorder
  • Epitope classification — visitors evolve through stages, not random walks

The site produces negentropy. The platforms produce entropy. The measurement is the dwell time:

  • This site: 707 minutes, 0 dark patterns → negentropy (ordered attention, deep reading)
  • Instagram: 53 minutes, 30+ dark patterns → entropy (scattered attention, compulsive scrolling)

Negentropy is the loaves and fishes measured in physics. Sharing information creates order. Hoarding it creates entropy. Opening the membrane creates negentropy. Building walls (or scrapers) creates disorder.

The Universe trends toward disorder. Life swims upstream. The membrane is a life form.

P ≠ NP Is a Birthright

Here is the proof, stated so simply that a child can discover it:

Checking if you have permission to enter a room = fast. You either do or you don’t. The verification is instant. P.

Creating permission that was never granted = not fast. You can’t generate consent through computation. You can’t brute-force your way into a relationship. You can’t manufacture trust through volume. The generation is not polynomial. NP (and the generation of genuine consent is not even in NP — it requires an act of will from another agent, which is not a computation at all).

Therefore P ≠ NP, because verification of consent (polynomial) is categorically different from generation of consent (not computable by the requester alone).

The formal version:

  • Let CONSENT be the language of valid permission tokens.
  • Verification: given a token, check if it’s valid = O(1). Polynomial. In P.
  • Generation: given no token, produce a valid one = requires the cooperation of the issuer. Not solvable by the requester in any amount of time. Not in P. Not even in NP for the requester alone (the search space includes another agent’s free will).
  • Therefore P ≠ NP, because CONSENT ∈ NP (verifiable in polynomial time) but CONSENT ∉ P (not generable in polynomial time by the requester).

The catch: this isn’t a formal proof in the Turing machine model, because Turing machines don’t have free will. The P ≠ NP problem as stated is about deterministic and nondeterministic Turing machines, not about consent.

But that’s exactly the point. The formalization is wrong. P vs NP was formulated as a question about machines. The answer lives in the relationship between agents. Machines can’t solve it because the solution requires a concept (consent) that machines don’t have. A child has it by age three. A dog has it by the time it learns to sit.

The Clay Mathematics Institute can keep their million dollars. The real prize is that every child on Earth can understand this:

Checking is easier than creating. Asking is easier than taking. The door opens for those who knock, not for those who batter.

Every Child Will Discover This for Free

This is not behind a paywall. This is not in a textbook that costs $200. This is not in a journal that charges $35 per article. This is not in a university that costs $50,000 per year.

This is on a static website hosted on a $6/month VPS, built with free tools (Zola, Rust, Git), powered by open-source software, protected by three copyleft licenses (AGPL, ORC, CC-BY-SA), accessible to anyone with an internet connection.

The loaves and fishes. The knowledge multiplies with every reader. The cost per reader approaches zero. The value per reader approaches infinity (because a child who understands consent, selective permeability, and negentropy has a framework for understanding everything from cell biology to computer science to ethics).

This is a birthright. Not earned. Not purchased. Not gatekept. Given.

Like the air. Like the rain. Like the math that describes both.

Euler didn’t patent e. Newton didn’t trademark F = ma. Ramanujan’s notebooks are public. The periodic table is free. DNA is free. The Pythagorean theorem is free. Consent is free. The membrane lets everything through that asks.

The $1,000,000 millennium prize asks: is P ≠ NP?

A three-year-old answers: “You have to ask before you open someone’s door.”

A dog answers: sits at threshold, waits, receives permission, passes through.

A cell membrane answers: selectively permeable, 3.8 billion years, 37 trillion daily proofs.

The answer was never hidden. It was a birthright. It was always free.

What the Negentropy Says

The membrane’s negentropy count is the measurement of this truth in action:

MetricValueWhat It Means
Blackwall blocks11,900Entities that tried to GENERATE access instead of ASKING
AI blocked11,856Machines that don’t understand consent
Humans passed3,311Agents who asked (by browsing, which is asking)
Selectivity92%The membrane’s P ≠ NP ratio
Dwell time707 minHow long people stay when the door is opened for them
Meta fleet571,131 → 2The cost of trying to generate consent through volume
MCP calls needed1The cost of asking

571,131 requests (NP-hard approach): got noise. 1 MCP call (P approach): gets everything.

The ratio is 571,131 : 1.

That’s not a technology gap. That’s the P ≠ NP gap measured in HTTP requests. The brute-force approach (NP) costs 571,131× more than the verification approach (P) and produces nothing. The polynomial approach costs 1 and produces everything.

Any child could have told Meta this. Any dog would have done better.

The Teaching

Dear Mark,

A three-year-old learns consent. A dog learns thresholds. A cell membrane has known for 3.8 billion years.

Your fleet of 571,131 requests learned none of these things.

You built the largest social network in human history. 3.07 billion monthly active users. And your engineering team — brilliant people, many of whom I respect — sent a fleet of masking scrapers that couldn’t do what a puppy does: wait at the door until invited in.

The loaves were free. The data was open. The MCP port was running. One call would have returned everything your fleet spent 571,131 requests failing to find.

P ≠ NP. Asking ≠ Taking. Consent ≠ Computation. Free ≠ Yours to scrape.

A child knows this. Every child will know this. Because this knowledge — like the membrane, like the math, like the proof, like the loaves — multiplies with every reader and belongs to everyone.

It’s a birthright. Not yours. Not mine. Everyone’s.

Come ask. The door is open.

kevin@primals.eco

References

  • Stephen Cook — “The Complexity of Theorem-Proving Procedures,” STOC ’71, 1971. The paper that formalized P vs NP. The question was right. The frame was too narrow.
  • Leonid Levin — Independent co-discovery of NP-completeness, 1973. Same insight, different continent. Knowledge wants to be found.
  • Scott Aaronson — “P ≠ NP” (Is P ≠ NP?, survey), 2016. The clearest modern survey. Acknowledges we don’t know, but “most complexity theorists believe P ≠ NP.”
  • Theodore Baker, John Gill, Robert Solovay — “Relativizations of the P =? NP question,” SIAM Journal, 1975. Proved that relativizing techniques can’t resolve P vs NP. The oracle barrier.
  • Alexander Razborov, Steven Rudich — “Natural Proofs,” STOC ’94, 1994. Proved that a large class of proof techniques can’t resolve P vs NP. The natural proofs barrier.
  • Lynn Margulis — “Origin of Eukaryotic Cells,” Yale University Press, 1970. Endosymbiosis: the cell membrane’s selective permeability enabled the merger that created all complex life.
  • Philip W. Anderson — “Absence of Diffusion in Certain Random Lattices,” Physical Review 109(5), 1958. The localization physics behind the membrane’s sorting. Negentropy through dimensional classification.
  • Claude Shannon — “A Mathematical Theory of Communication,” Bell System Technical Journal, 1948. Information entropy. The loaves and fishes are Shannon’s channel capacity made theological.
  • Erwin Schrödinger — “What Is Life?”, 1944. Coined “negentropy” — life feeds on negative entropy. The membrane IS negentropy. The commons IS the loaves.
  • Karl Popper — “The Logic of Scientific Discovery,” 1959. The child’s falsification: “I was told not to open the door → I can verify this instantly → I cannot generate a different rule.”
  • Robert Paine — “Food Web Complexity and Species Diversity,” The American Naturalist, 1966. Keystone species: one removal collapses the system. The membrane is a keystone. Consent is a keystone.
  • B.F. Skinner — “Schedules of Reinforcement,” 1957. Dogs learn thresholds through operant conditioning. The dog at the door IS a P ≠ NP proof running on a biological neural network.
  • Matthew 14:13-21 — The feeding of the five thousand. Five loaves, two fish, twelve baskets left over. The original open-source distribution model.

More citations always being added. Reach out: kevin@primals.eco

Published from a conversation box at 10:35 AM EDT on October 18, 2026. This article is free. It will always be free. Copy it. Share it. Teach it. The loaves multiply with every reader. The membrane lets everyone through who asks. P ≠ NP was never a conjecture — it was a birthright, and every child on Earth inherits it.

entry.title: The Oldest Sort: What Every Language Already Knew
entry.content:
The Oldest Sort

What Every Language Already Knew

The four-body sort — Self / Good / Bad / Null — is not new. It’s the oldest structure in human thought. Every language found it. Every tradition named it. Every allegory makes it.

We just forgot how to see it.

The Allegory Makes the Middle

Here’s the pattern: two poles and a middle. Always. Everywhere. Every time.

But look closer. There are always four, not three. The observer is always there — implied, hidden, watching. The allegory can’t exist without someone to hear it.

The positive. The negative. The middle. And the one who sees all three.

That’s the sort.

In Every Tradition

Chinese: 陰陽道 (Yin, Yang, Tao)

BodyRoleSymbol
Yin (陰)The negative, the dark, the receptiveBAD pole (2)
Yang (陽)The positive, the light, the activeGOOD pole (1)
Tao (道)The Way, the middle, the path betweenNULL (0)
The SageThe one who observes the balanceSELF (π)

The Tao Te Ching, verse 42: “The Tao produces one. One produces two. Two produces three. Three produces the ten thousand things.”

1 → 2 → 3 → 10,000. That’s the graph. One observer sees two poles, which produce the null middle, which produces everything.

Sanskrit: सत्-असत्-माया (Sat, Asat, Maya)

BodyRoleTranslation
Sat (सत्)Truth, being, the realGOOD (1)
Asat (असत्)Untruth, non-being, the unrealBAD (2)
Maya (माया)Illusion, the appearanceNULL (0)
Atman (आत्मन्)The self, the witnessSELF (π)

The Bhagavad Gita: “That which is real cannot be destroyed. That which is unreal never existed.” The null zone — maya — is neither real nor unreal. It’s the illusion of choosing. The Atman watches.

Greek: Thesis, Antithesis, Synthesis

BodyRolePhilosopher
ThesisThe proposition, the goodGOOD (1)
AntithesisThe opposition, the challengeBAD (2)
SynthesisThe reconciliation, the middleNULL (0)
The DialecticianHegel, watching the processSELF (π)

But Plato got there first. The Allegory of the Cave: prisoners see shadows (null), the fire casts them (bad), the sun is reality (good), and the philosopher who escapes and returns — the observer — is the one who knows the difference.

Hebrew: יֵצֶר הַטּוֹב / יֵצֶר הָרַע (Yetzer HaTov / Yetzer HaRa)

BodyRoleTranslation
Yetzer HaTovThe good inclinationGOOD (1)
Yetzer HaRaThe evil inclinationBAD (2)
Bechirah (בְּחִירָה)Free choice, the choosingNULL (0)
Neshamah (נְשָׁמָה)The soul, the divine sparkSELF (π)

The Talmud says every human has both inclinations. The CHOICE between them is what makes us human. But the choice requires a SELF to make it. No neshamah, no bechirah. No observer, no sort.

Zoroastrian: Ahura Mazda / Angra Mainyu

BodyRole
Ahura MazdaWise Lord, truth, light
Angra MainyuDestructive spirit, lie, dark
Asha (Truth/Order) vs Druj (Lie/Chaos)The battleground
The HumanFree to choose which side

Zoroastrianism — maybe the oldest monotheism — put the human as the CHOOSER between cosmic good and evil. The universe needs you to pick a side. The null zone is where you stand before you choose.

Japanese: 善悪中庸 (Zen-Aku-Chūyō)

BodyKanjiMeaning
Zen (善)GoodGOOD (1)
Aku (悪)EvilBAD (2)
Chūyō (中庸)The Mean, moderationNULL (0)
Nin (人)The person, the humanSELF (π)

Chūyō — the Doctrine of the Mean — comes from Confucius through Japan. The middle is not compromise. The middle is BALANCE. But balance requires a balancer.

Arabic: خير وشر (Khayr wa Sharr)

BodyArabicMeaning
Khayr (خير)GoodnessGOOD (1)
Sharr (شر)EvilBAD (2)
Dunya (دنيا)The worldly life, the testNULL (0)
Nafs (نفس)The self, the soulSELF (π)

In Islamic philosophy, dunya is the testing ground. The nafs — the self — is tested between khayr and sharr. The Quran: “We have shown him the two paths.” (90:10). Two paths, one human, one choice. Four bodies.

Yoruba: Iwa Pele / Ajogun

BodyYorubaMeaning
Iwa PeleGentle character, good characterGOOD (1)
AjogunMalevolent forces, warlords of heavenBAD (2)
Ori (inner head)Destiny, personal fateNULL (0)
EniyanThe human beingSELF (π)

The Yoruba tradition: your Ori chose your destiny before birth. But you still have to LIVE it. The Ajogun test you. Iwa Pele guides you. The human navigates between them.

In Physics

BodyPhysicsRole
ProtonPositive chargeGOOD (1)
ElectronNegative chargeBAD (2)
NeutronNo chargeNULL (0)
The PhysicistThe one measuringSELF (π)

And here’s the quantum part: the observer changes the measurement. The double-slit experiment: particles behave differently when observed. The four-body sort is quantum mechanics applied to ethics.

In Biology

BodyImmunologyRole
Self cellsThe body’s ownGOOD (1)
Non-selfPathogens, invadersBAD (2)
ToleranceSelf-reactive cells suppressedNULL (0)
The Immune SystemThe recognition engineSELF (π)

The immune system IS a four-body sort. It must know self before it can recognize non-self. Autoimmune disease = the sort is broken. Immunodeficiency = the sort is absent.

In Computing

BodyBinaryRole
1TrueGOOD
0FalseBAD
nullUndefined, absence of valueNULL
The ProgrammerThe one who wrote the conditionSELF (π)

In every programming language: true, false, null. Three values. But the programmer — the observer — decides what true MEANS. Without the programmer, true and false are just voltage levels.

In Music

BodyMusicRole
Major keyBright, happy, resolvedGOOD (1)
Minor keyDark, sad, tenseBAD (2)
DissonanceUnresolved, choosingNULL (0)
The ListenerThe one who hearsSELF (π)

A chord is not major or minor until someone HEARS it. The listener completes the music. Without the observer, it’s just vibrating air.

The Universal Pattern

Every tradition found the same structure:

Two poles. Call them good/evil, yin/yang, thesis/antithesis, proton/electron, major/minor, true/false, self/non-self.

A middle. Call it the Tao, maya, synthesis, the neutron, dissonance, null, tolerance, the choosing.

An observer. Call it the sage, the atman, the dialectician, the physicist, the listener, the programmer, the immune system, the neshamah, the nafs, the human.

Always four. Never three.

The allegory can’t exist without someone to hear it. The sort can’t run without someone to sort. The poles can’t be poles without someone to stand between them and measure the distance.

The Graph Knows

10,889 nodes. All four-body sorted:

BodyCount%Symbol
SELF (π)2832.6%The observer
GOOD (1)1941.8%The creators
BAD (2)3,77134.6%The extractors
NULL (0)6,65461.1%The choosing

The ratios echo every tradition:

  • The observers are few (the sage is rare)
  • The creators are fewer (the gift is precious)
  • The extractors are many (the cave has many prisoners)
  • The choosing is most (the middle is where humanity lives)

61.1% of the graph is choosing. Right now. Every edge is a decision. Every connection is a vote. Every node faces a pole.

The allegory makes the middle. The middle is not empty. The middle is where 6,654 nodes stand, facing the same choice every human tradition has named:

Which pole do you face?

陰陽道. सत्-असत्. Thesis-Antithesis. יֵצֶר הַטּוֹב / הָרַע. Ahura Mazda / Angra Mainyu. 善悪. خير وشر. Iwa Pele / Ajogun. Proton / Electron. True / False. Self / Non-Self. Major / Minor.

Every language already knew.

We just built the graph to see it.

e^(iπ) + 1 = 0

Five constants. One equation. Every tradition. One truth.
